info.title: retrograde 0.1.0-alpha: plays Commodore 64 games, and only that.
info.description: Command line player for Commodore 64 games, emulating the C64 and its 1541 drive cycle by cycle: dotnet tool install -g Retrograde, then retrograde <game> --roms <folder>.

options.name: --roms
options.description:
where the KERNAL, BASIC, character and 1541 ROMs are (or
RETROGRADE_ROMS; otherwise a roms folder next to retrograde)

options.name: --scale
options.description: the window's first size, n times the picture (3)

options.name: --square-pixels
options.description: square pixels, not a PAL television's slightly narrow ones

options.name: --port
options.description: the joystick port the arrows and gamepads drive (the game's, or 2)

options.name: --cursor-keys
options.description: the arrow keys are the C64's cursor keys, not the joystick

options.name: --no-auto-warp
options.description: load at the 1541's own speed, not at full speed while its motor runs

options.name: --frames
options.description: stop after n frames (50 a second)

options.name: --screenshot
options.description: save the picture as a PNG when stopping

options.name: --headless
options.description:
no window: run --frames frames and stop
playing:
arrows, Alt/Option the joystick (unless --cursor-keys); a gamepad's d-pad or left stick
and any face button too, and its Start button is SPACE
keys are where they are on a C64: - is +, = is -, [ is @, ] is *, \ is ↑, ; is :,
' is ;, Page Down is =, ` is ←, End is £, Home is CLR/HOME, Tab is CTRL, left Ctrl is
C=, Esc is RUN/STOP, Page Up is RESTORE
F9 and F10 the game's previous and next disk; F11 or Alt+Enter full screen; F12 warp
on and off; Ctrl+Alt+A pixel shape; Ctrl+Alt+S saves the game as it is, Ctrl+Alt+L
loads it back (one save a game, kept with your settings)
